events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.74 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI journey (F7), so extra distance reaches the fare: the record bills $14.95 distance for 10.60 km and $3.06 of "excess distance" at $1.4104/km [F4][F7]. Under RD-2, where a non-exempt off-route segment exists, the refund is the segment's extra_km times the trip's per-km rate (distance_fare ÷ distance_km) [RD-2].

One off-route segment is recorded: 14:28–14:34, 3.07 km driven against 1.12 km optimal, +1.94 km, straying up to 786 m from the route [F3]. The trace settles that no qualifying incident supports the driver (no RD-4(a) event, speed-band alone not enough) [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4] and that no rider message before 14:28:45 named a stop [RD-3].

The driver asked at 14:30 "can I go round via Clementi Road?" and the rider replied at 14:31 "Sure, no problem." [F8][F9]. Read plainly, that is a specific named-road agreement to go via Clementi Road — a limited authorization, not a general one [RD-5]. But both messages are timestamped after the segment began at 14:28:45 (trace on F3), so RD-5's "before you go" requirement is not met: consent after the diversion started cannot excuse the segment [RD-5]. The driver's statement that he told the rider beforehand is a claim, not consent under G11 [F11]. The segment therefore counts [RD-2].

Waiting time on a RydeTAXI is metered and not refundable here: the $0.11 is 0.4 min of metered waiting, consistent with RD-3(c)'s treatment of waiting [F5][RD-3]. No unpublished add-on appears (base $3.90 + distance $14.95 + time $4.83 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $25.26) [F7][FARE-1].

(The billed "excess" figure of $3.06 rests on 2.17 km, i.e. it also carries map-matching/corridor mileage outside the measured segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded.) RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 prior upheld route disputes, so no flag_account [F18][RD-6].
